bullets.title: S&P +1.2% weekly but breadth collapsed to 2nd-percentile historic lows
bullets.body: Despite SPX gaining 1.2% on the week and touching fresh records early, fewer than 30% of constituents outperformed—the second-weakest breadth reading since 2005. Mag-7 (GOOGL +2.4%, MSFT +3.4%, TSLA +3.3%, AMZN +4.3%) masked broad deterioration: 75% of S&P 500 stocks are down since mid-August and NYSE new lows outnumbered new highs 85% of the time over 28 consecutive sessions. Systematic macro leverage sits at the 80th 5-year percentile, limiting incremental buying power.

bullets.title: Q3 earnings season opens with SPX forecasting +29.5% EPS growth; bar is high
bullets.body: Consensus expects 12.3% revenue growth, 29.5% EPS growth, and 15% margins (second-best quarter ever) for 3Q26, with all 11 sectors in positive territory. Goldman estimates median S&P 500 stock EPS growth of 9%, well below the index's AI-skewed headline. Large-cap banks (C, GS, JPM, WFC) kick off Tuesday; TSMC and ASML report later in the week. Positive pre-announcement count is at a record high, but the bar has rarely been higher.

bullets.title: Fed signals December hike live; October hold odds fell to 22% post-FOMC minutes
bullets.body: Fed Governor Waller pivoted hawkish, stating 'labor market is stable and inflation is too high' and flagging December and March hikes as appropriate without requiring consecutive meetings. FOMC minutes showed October hike probability declining from 64% to 22% and December from 84% to 78%. Prediction markets price 74% odds of a 25bp December hike; 10-year yields range-traded near 5.24-5.35% on the week. September core CPI (next Wednesday) is the key near-term catalyst, with MS forecasting +0.24% m/m (down from +0.29%).

bullets.title: 10-year yields at 5.25%+ flagged as restrictive but potentially new normal
bullets.body: Multiple strategists debated whether 5%+ rates represent overshoot or new equilibrium. Wolfe notes 10-year above 5%, mortgage rates above 7%, yet unemployment at 4.2% and GDP growing healthily. 22V Research upgraded its non-inflationary growth ceiling to 2.25% from 2.0%, implying $4-5T additional cumulative output over a decade. Michigan 1-year inflation expectations came in at 4.7% vs 4.8% consensus; core PCE was revised down 36bp, easing one key headwind for inflation markets.

bullets.title: Hedge funds net-sold Info Tech at -1.0 SD after buying it 4 of past 5 weeks; rotated into Industrials
bullets.body: Goldman Prime shows Info Tech was the most net sold US sector this week (-1.0 SDs 1-year) after being the most net bought in 4 of the prior 5 weeks. Short sales outpaced long buys 1.3-to-1 globally. Industrials and Consumer Discretionary were the most net bought sectors. Fundamental L/S funds fell -0.70% vs MSCI World +0.78%, hurt by alpha losses on both sides; Systematic L/S gained +0.82%.

bullets.title: AI CapEx sustainability debate intensifies: $400-600B ARR threshold by end-2027 is the key marker
bullets.body: 22V Research, JPM, and multiple sell-side notes converged on the view that $400-600B in aggregate AI-lab ARR exiting 2027 is the minimum needed to justify capex plans through 2028-29 and avoid a 2029 spending cliff. OpenAI clarified its $50B September run-rate (net, not gross) and confirmed a $70B year-end target, reversing Thursday's selloff. Compute rental pricing surged to $25-50M per megawatt from $10-12M six months ago—a move sell-side models have not captured. 54% of surveyed investors cite Chinese AI model price competition as a key risk.

bullets.title: AI infrastructure debt boom: SpaceX $40B, Broadcom $50B+, Oracle raising GPU purchase financing
bullets.body: Hyperscaler and frontier-lab AI chip financing is becoming a distinct capital-markets theme. SpaceX is raising ~$40B ($10B bank loans, $30B IG debt) to buy NVIDIA GPUs; Broadcom arranged $50B+ for OpenAI's custom chip buildout and $60B for Anthropic; Oracle is in talks with Apollo and Goldman for large GPU purchase financing. NVIDIA announced a $500B third-party capital pool for AI compute financing. French CDS and NVDA CDS are trading at essentially the same levels per GS—a striking sign of how AI credit risk is being priced.

bullets.title: SpaceX acquires $8B 800MHz low-band spectrum—fourth wireless carrier threat drives telcos down 10%+
bullets.body: SpaceX agreed to buy a nationwide 800MHz spectrum portfolio from Grain Management for ~$8B (~$1.70/MHz-PoP), enabling a satellite-terrestrial hybrid Starlink Mobile service. T-Mobile fell 12.1%, AT&T 9.9%, Verizon 10.3% in heavy put-heavy options trading. Tower stocks (CCI +7.8%, SBAC +7.6%, AMT +6%) rallied on the expectation that SpaceX will need 60-70K macro sites. Morgan Stanley models less than 1% US mobile penetration by 2030 but growing to ~7% by 2035, initially rural-focused. FCC approved SpaceX's Gen2 constellation (15,000 satellites).

bullets.title: Semis (SOX -4.3%) vs Software (IGV +3.9%): ~800bps spread on the week
bullets.body: Heavy selling in the semis/AI complex Thursday-Friday on OpenAI revenue headline confusion drove the SOX down 4.3% and memory (DRAM) down 7.4%, while software (IGV) outperformed by roughly 800bps. PC shipments fell 20.1% YoY to 62.7M units in 3Q—the sharpest decline since COVID pull-ins unwound. Hedge funds rotated out of Info Tech and into Industrials, reversing September trends. Nasdaq funding premium to S&P reached the 98th 1-year percentile.

bullets.title: MRVL Investor Day raised FY28 to $20B and FY31 to $70-90B; custom silicon now includes Google
bullets.body: Marvell raised FY28 revenue guidance from ~$18B to $20B and introduced a FY31 framework of $70-90B (55-60% CAGR) with $30+ EPS, implying ~10x revenue growth from FY26. Custom silicon revenue target raised to $12B+ in FY29 (up from $10B) and $30B by FY31, now including Google. Interconnect TAM forecast to reach $65B by CY2030 at 65% CAGR. Stock was +8% intraday during the event. TD Cowen upgraded to Buy, Piper Sandler raised PT to $400.

bullets.title: CEG +8-10% on 890MW new nuclear + 2.7GW PPA deal with Google; IPPs re-rated as AI-power beneficiaries
bullets.body: Constellation Energy signed a 20-year, 890MW new nuclear capacity deal with Google plus a 15-year 2.7GW existing capacity PPA, representing $4.3B+ in new Constellation investment. The deal is the third major PJM power contract without a 1-for-1 new generation requirement in 2026. IPPs (TLN, VST) rallied ~15% on average as data-center power was validated as a real, monetizable constraint. UBS notes power infrastructure positioning is in the 3rd percentile with normalized valuations after summer correction.

bullets.title: Meta Muse AI agent: #1 US App Store 22 consecutive days, 6.6M+ downloads; marketplace fears appear overdone
bullets.body: Meta's Muse personal AI agent topped the US App Store for 22 straight days with 6.6M+ downloads and 1.8M DAUs, including an expansion to iPad. Wolfe Research projects a $30-50B long-term revenue opportunity via subscriptions and take-rate monetization, with Year 1 scenarios at $8B. Marketplace stocks (EXPE, BKNG, DASH, SHOP, UBER) sold off 15-25% on agentic AI fears, but most sell-side analysis concludes the risk profile looks modest: only 27% of consumers have tried Muse and 64% won't trust agents with credit cards. Amazon blocked Muse.

bullets.title: Agentic AI threatens OTA commission pools; BKNG, ABNB, EXPE down 15-25% YTD as agents book directly
bullets.body: Hedgeye and multiple other firms flagged that Meta's Muse and Google's hotel booking in AI Mode now complete bookings without OTA or hotel integration, using browser automation and one-time cards. Payment and merchant-of-record bottlenecks that previously blocked the thesis have largely been removed in North America. None of the 11 tracked OTA/hotel brands allow outside agents to complete bookings independently. Hotels and consumers are positioned to benefit while OTA commission pools face deflationary pressure.

bullets.title: Brazil election: Bolsonaro leads runoff with 6%+ margin; LatAm equities re-rated
bullets.body: Flávio Bolsonaro entered the October 25 runoff with a clear advantage (47% vs Lula 45.2%), and his party (PL) had its strongest congressional showing in decades, potentially enabling fiscal adjustment via constitutional measures. JPMorgan upgraded Brazil to Overweight and upgraded BRL to Overweight, targeting USD/BRL 4.70-4.80. MSCI Brazil is at 8.9x forward P/E vs a potential re-rating toward 10.9x. BofA remains overweight Brazil, noting the Ibovespa reached 14x P/E in the Bolsonaro era vs 9.4x currently.

bullets.title: EU-China trade tensions: managed agreement emerging on hybrid vehicles and rare earths
bullets.body: EU trade talks with China produced a joint statement showing modest progress on hybrid vehicle tariff rate quotas and rare earth export facilitation, postponing escalation past the October 15 EU summit. Germany shifted position after Chinese competitive pressure accelerated, with the Federation of German Industry now supporting confrontation. France and Germany proposed expanding EU trade defense tools for sector-wide rapid retaliation. China has demonstrated 'trade escalation dominance' and is unlikely to accept new demands without testing EU resolve.

bullets.title: Euro area growth cut to 1.0% in 3Q26; France political risk elevated, Germany near stagnation
bullets.body: JPMorgan cut its Euro area 3Q GDP forecast by 25bp to 1.0% annualized, with Germany slashed 1.0 point to 0.25% on retail sales down 7.5% and manufacturing contracting 6.5%. France lowered to 0.5%; Spain unchanged at 3.0%. French fiscal plan lacks concrete measures and spreads reverted within 24 hours of initial relief. UBS hosted a call flagging French OAT sustainability risk with Le Pen's €140B savings plan relying on implausibly low fiscal multipliers. ECB expected to cut planned hikes from four to three by end-2027.

bullets.title: Oil rallied Thursday on Middle East tensions; crude-rates decoupling noted as 10-year fell
bullets.body: WTI rose on Strait of Hormuz tensions and Middle East escalation signals while Treasury yields fell—a notable decoupling. Brent at $99 with a Hedgeye risk range of $96-$106. Jefferies geopolitical analysis notes the conflict transmission mechanism is shifting from physical crude scarcity to inflation, Treasury yields, bond volatility, and financial conditions. Trump signaled no pre-midterm Iran strikes (WTI +0.8% on the news). Goldman is bullish across E&P, power/LNG, refining, and natural gas upstream with 10 stocks averaging 27% total return potential.

bullets.title: VIX upside convexity extremely bid; SPX downside protection offered; vol could rise to low-20s on hot CPI
bullets.body: Options market structure entering Q3 earnings season is asymmetric: VIX upside convexity is extremely bid while SPX downside convexity remains very offered per MS QDS. Customer S&P 500 put delta positioning shifted to net supply, limiting downside protection. A rise in realized vol from 10% to 15% could trigger ~$90B of equity supply from systematic funds. Dealers are short gamma in Russell 2000 (RTY), amplifying potential upside moves. Retail flows collapsed to $22B (19th 1-year percentile), historically a leading indicator of subsequent weakness.

bullets.title: US midterm elections: Dems >90% odds for House net gain of 3+ seats, 65% for Senate majority
bullets.body: Prediction markets imply >90% probability Democrats net at least 3 House seats, and 65% probability of a Democratic Senate majority. A divided government would retain Trump administration authority over tariffs, foreign policy, and deregulation, but data centers face greater permitting scrutiny under a Democratic House. Healthcare services and managed care benefit from greater Democratic Medicaid leverage. Hedgeye flags Texas gubernatorial race tightening as the biggest risk to AI buildout names given Texas hosts ~35-40% of announced IT capacity through 2030.
